what: The source-built transient_accept_errors_leave_the_reactor_available_to_healthy_clients test failed after 19.176238 seconds with a raw Io(Again), while 124 other local protocol tests passed. The original production artifact records no socket syscalls; it does not establish the cause of the post-connect handshake failure.
cost: The local protocol acceptance failed and the observer did not run the wire or serve packages.
cause: The fault-injection fixture races an independently started server against Client's five-second handshake IO timeouts. It did not separately observe the injected accept failures before asserting a healthy welcome.
whys: The fixture used a full concurrent client handshake to test an accept-error classification.
The production reactor exposed only its unbounded run loop, so a fixture could not drive one real iteration.
The assertion therefore combined accept recovery with server startup, thread scheduling and source-compiled first-call work. The retained trace cannot apportion those costs.
class: A fault-injection control depends on unrelated wall-clock startup before it observes the injected transition.
prevention: The production loop delegates its unchanged tick, accept, read and write ordering to one turn. The test drives exactly three injected transient errors with a real hello already queued, proves the welcome reaches the peer, rejects a fatal error, and checks cancellation before another turn. Existing concurrent Client/server controls remain in tests/unix.rs.
workaround: None: no additional timeout, retry, ignored test or substituted protocol implementation.
fix: One-turn fixture and fatal-error/cancellation controls passed native ARM64 and source-built execution in run 46120488242, tree fe3859b920da54c052a8ff788f5546a81bec397b. All 392 source-built distributed protocol tests and 112 required controls executed successfully. The old handshake failure's underlying timing cause remains unproven; the narrower fixture now observes its own injected transition directly.
